solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flipping balanced by means of self-control

indicators.note: something flipped is turned over, so the next word is read from its last letter back

parts.note: two sums that balance have met, matched each other exactly
per is Latin for by means of, as in per post

explanation.surface: Someone balanced with flipping self-control, a mild oath in the middle of a calm temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British oath, but it turns the word for balanced around.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep or lose your temper is to keep or lose your composure, so temper is calm restraint.

clue.text: This bores trustee of estate, amongst others

parts.note: tr is an abbreviation for trustee
o is short for of, as in o'clock
an estate is one kind of car

explanation.surface: A dull trustee of an estate, boring others as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' suggests tedium but means drills; 'amongst others' signals an estate is just one type of car.
explanation.definitionFit: A trocar is a surgical instrument with a sharp point used to pierce body cavities.

clue.text: Public showing unerring openness to danger

parts.note: an expo is an exhibition
a sure shot never misses

explanation.surface: A public display of confidence that reveals vulnerability.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is the state of being unprotected, laid open to harm or risk.

clue.text: Clubman potting two in the middle in an old sort of pool

indicators.note: potting a ball in snooker sinks it from the table, so letters are removed

parts.note: a club's man is a member
the central pair of letters

explanation.surface: A club regular potting two balls mid-table in an old-fashioned pool game.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a game of pool at the club; the pool is actually water and potting removes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Meer is an old spelling of mere, a lake or pond.

clue.text: Secretly plot against losing count — this shows him for what he is

definitions.text: this shows him for what he is

indicators.note: losing a word means it drops away from the front of the longer one

parts.note: to countermine is to plot covertly against a plan
taken as written: the part removed

explanation.surface: Someone plotting secretly against a count, whose robes reveal his true nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Him' refers to the count: the definition leans on the wordplay word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine fur trims the robes of peers, so it marks a nobleman's rank.

clue.text: People who build? Perhaps wet, perhaps cut-throat, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, not spelt

parts.note: wet shaving and cut-throat are both types of shaving blade

explanation.surface: Are builders a bit drippy, or ruthless?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' and 'cut-throat' look like character judgements but describe kinds of shaving blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder raises walls and houses, so the question mark flags a loose sense of raisers.

clue.text: Sloth, whose life is carefree, wasting energy in an offhand way

parts.note: the ai is the three-toed sloth

indicators.note: wasting something means losing it, so a letter drops out of the carefree word

parts.note: to live the life of Riley is to live without care
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lazy creature living without cares wastes energy and behaves casually.
explanation.walkthrough: AI, the three-toed sloth, is a crossword staple; Riley loses his E.
explanation.definitionFit: Airily describes acting lightly and without concern, which is a casual, offhand manner.

clue.text: We decorate policewomen clearing off

indicators.note: clearing a word off removes it, leaving what remains

parts.note: police officers

explanation.surface: Policewomen tidying up say they put up the decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person plural: cake decorators would say 'we decorate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Icers are people who ice cakes, decorating them with icing.

clue.text: Mudlark, once, with extra good music

indicators.note: an extra letter is slipped into the word

parts.note: a mudlark was a street urchin, a ragged child
G is short for good

explanation.surface: A street urchin of old, with some fine music.
explanation.walkthrough: Mudlarks scavenged the Thames mud; a ragamuffin spelt with one G becomes the music with two.
explanation.definitionFit: Raggamuffin, or ragga, is a style of Jamaican dancehall music.

clue.text: Italy claims to totter with respect to monotheism

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: something tottering is unsteady, so its letters wobble out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Italy's claims about belief in one god are shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is a monotheistic faith, so Islamic means relating to that belief in one God.

clue.text: Yankee feature of some columns is lacking gossips

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so that word drops out

parts.note: entasis is the slight swelling of a classical column
taken as written: the part removed

explanation.surface: An American architectural feature is missing, say the busybodies.
explanation.walkthrough: Entasis is the gentle convex curve given to Greek columns.
explanation.definitionFit: Yenta is Yiddish for a gossip or busybody.

clue.text: We've entire gathering to introduce one applicant

indicators.note: to introduce something is to put it in
a gathering collects things loosely together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The whole team has assembled to welcome one job hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant for a job is usually interviewed, so the candidate is the interviewee.

clue.text: Fish favoured by French chefs scares easily when captured

indicators.note: something captured is held inside, so one piece sits within the other
taken as loosely, without effort, so the word's letters fall into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
as and when both mean at the time that

explanation.surface: A fish that French cooks love is easily frightened when caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The rascasse, or scorpion fish, is a classic ingredient of bouillabaisse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascasse is the Mediterranean scorpion fish, essential to the Provençal fish stew bouillabaisse.

clue.text: Come in and start to perform freely, it's such an event

definitions.text: Come in and start to perform freely, it's such an event

indicators.note: letters set free are no longer bound to their printed order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the first letter of perform

explanation.surface: An invitation to walk in and do a turn without restriction, which is exactly what such a night offers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the event while its words also build it: anyone may come in and perform.
explanation.definitionFit: An open mic night is a session where members of the public can drop in and take a turn on stage.

clue.text: Some panel games overturned depression

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so the letters run backwards
only some of the letters of the words that follow are used, sitting in a row

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Some TV panel games were cancelled, causing gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low spirits, but here it is a dip in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow Scottish valley, a depression in the landscape.

clue.text: This lets you hear cornet trio's set, once started

parts.note: cor is a dictionary abbreviation for cornet

indicators.note: to set something is to arrange it, so the letters are placed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
gan is an archaic past tense meaning began

explanation.surface: A brass trio's performance begins, and you can hear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a musical set but is the rearranging signal; gan is old usage for began.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of Corti in the cochlea of the inner ear holds the hair cells that turn sound into nerve signals.

clue.text: Poplar is, to whatever extent, cooler

parts.note: as in as much as you like: to whatever degree
the cooler is slang for prison, as is the pen (penitentiary)

explanation.surface: A poplar tree is, however much, a cooling presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like a comparison of temperature but is slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a species of poplar known for its trembling leaves.

clue.text: Being nuts about British Airways, Tibetans get stuck into it

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: mast is the nuts of beech and oak trees fallen on the ground
the airline's initials

explanation.surface: Mad about a British airline, Tibetan passengers tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' suggests crazy but is beech mast; 'get stuck into' is British slang for eating heartily.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsamba is roasted barley flour, the staple food of Tibet, eaten as a dough with butter tea.

clue.text: Upset dweeb, beset by worry, moaned

indicators.note: beset by something means surrounded by it, so one piece is placed within
something upset is knocked over, its letters disarranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to ail is to trouble or worry

explanation.surface: An upset nerd, plagued by anxiety, complained.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the worry is inside the nerd's letters rather than surrounding them, a reversal of what 'beset by' suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewail is to lament loudly, so bewailed means moaned.

clue.text: Stumped by short story competition

parts.note: a conte is a short story
st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: Puzzled by a short story competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumped' looks like puzzled but is the cricket dismissal, a way the wicketkeeper puts a batter out.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest is a competition between rivals.

clue.text: Fights with Scots before noon, I'm back breaking resolution

indicators.note: letters breaking into a word split it open and sit inside

parts.note: res is the abbreviation for resolution
a.m. is ante meridiem, before noon

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the contraction is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone back from Scotland before noon, scuffling, has broken a resolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With Scots' marks the definition as Scottish usage; RES must be split open to hold the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Rammy is a Scots word for a noisy brawl or free-for-all, so rammies are fights.

clue.text: Greek goddess, she's flat out painting place

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
one lying flat out is a lier

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess lies flat, posing in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She's flat out' suggests exhausted but describes someone lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's studio or workshop.

clue.text: For some colleges, head for Old Street after 5

parts.note: pro means in favour of
V is the Roman numeral five
O is the abbreviation for old
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Directions to some colleges: make for Old Street after five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head for' reads as one phrase meaning go to, but it splits: head is the definition, for is the first piece. Old Street is a London street and station.
explanation.definitionFit: Provost is the title of the head of several colleges, such as Eton and King's College, Cambridge.

clue.text: Promise pickle, ploughman's tip — easy to get down

parts.note: first meaning: to ... your troth is to pledge it
second meaning: a predicament

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very first letter

parts.note: the first letter of ploughman's
a light meal is easy to digest

explanation.surface: A ploughman's lunch with pickle promises to be easily eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings plus a charade: a ploughman's is a British pub lunch of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Plight means both to pledge solemnly and a difficult situation or predicament.

clue.text: Mean to pack article used by Spaniard's instrument

indicators.note: packing something means putting it inside

parts.note: mean and vile both mean nasty
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A stingy Spaniard packs his musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A vielle is a medieval stringed instrument, an early fiddle or hurdy-gurdy.

clue.text: American's poor take for Newton's clockwork model

indicators.note: one thing stands for another, so a letter is swapped in place

parts.note: ornery is American for inferior or poor
R stands for recipe, Latin take, on prescriptions
N is the symbol for newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: An American's poor attempt at Newton's clockwork model of the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newton' suggests the scientist but is the unit of force; 'take' is the R of a prescription.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system showing the planets' motions.

clue.text: In supposedly significant line fool finds forbearance

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: a ley line is supposed to have mystical significance
nit is short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A fool on a mystical ley line discovers patience.
explanation.walkthrough: Ley lines are alignments of ancient sites that some believe carry earth energies.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenity is mildness or leniency, the patient tolerance meant by forbearance.

clue.text: Erected facility for Cousteau and fish

indicators.note: in a down entry something erected stands upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: art is skill or facility
et is French for and; Cousteau was a French ocean explorer

explanation.surface: A facility built for the diver Cousteau and his fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Cousteau the oceanographer fits the fish surface but only signals French.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: ____ provided that end of fast (Arabic)

parts.note: if means on condition that

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of fast
Ar is the abbreviation for Arabic

explanation.surface: A sentence with a blank to fill: something provided the end of the fast, and the word is Arabic.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the answer in the blank and the clue reads as its own definition: the iftar provided the end of the fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Iftar is the evening meal with which Muslims break the daily fast during Ramadan; the word comes from Arabic.

clue.text: French article likely after dear old clergyman's market

indicators.note: placing words after another sends them second, so the word for dear comes first

parts.note: a steep price is a dear one
le is French for the
a fair chance is a likely one

explanation.surface: A French item that will probably follow a costly old vicar's market.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read in reverse clue order: 'after dear' puts the French article and likely after the word for dear.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple fair was an old term for a market where clergy could be hired, the steeple standing for the church.

clue.text: One type of current Middle East crisis that's forgotten

parts.note: alternating current
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A current Middle East crisis has been forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's forgotten' marks an obsolete sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Acme once meant the crisis or turning point of a disease, a medical sense now obsolete.

clue.text: Northern racer finding reward in part

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is needed, a run of letters within it

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A racer from the North gets part of the prize money.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle two words: the end of 'finding' and the start of 'reward'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grew is a Northern dialect word for a greyhound, a dog bred for racing.

clue.text: Fruit ices I'll supply

indicators.note: read as supplely, bending flexibly, so the letters are bent into another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A vendor promises to provide fruit ices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not the verb to provide but an adverb, in a supple manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A silicle is a short broad seed pod, the botanical fruit of plants like honesty and shepherd's purse.

clue.text: Stop, slyly look back on what's odd in shed — it's a gardener's thing

parts.note: ho is an old call to stop or halt

indicators.note: the odd letters are the first, third and so on

parts.note: first and third letters of shed

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to leer is to look slyly

explanation.surface: Stop, glance back slyly at the strange thing in the shed — a gardening gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's odd' sounds like something strange but means the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hose reel is the drum a garden hose is wound onto, standard gardening equipment.

clue.text: RIP or the equivalent in black

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: tar is black
o.t.e. is the abbreviation for or the equivalent, seen in job adverts

explanation.surface: An epitaph with mourning dress: Rest In Peace, or its equivalent, in black.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP looks like the epitaph but is the verb to rip, written in capitals to mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip and to tear are synonyms: both mean to pull something apart roughly.

clue.text: Prepared yours truly for a restorative

indicators.note: one thing in place of another, so a letter is swapped out

parts.note: prepared and ready are synonyms
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
the letter taken out

explanation.surface: A cook got something ready for a tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: ME replaces the A of the word for prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a medicine or cure, something that restores health.
